name: refactor_django_duplicate_views
description: Consolidates two copy-pasted CSV export views into one helper
prompts: shop/views.py has two CSV export views (export_books_csv and export_authors_csv) that duplicate the same response-building boilerplate: constructing the HttpResponse with the text/csv content type, setting the Content-Disposition attachment header, creating the csv writer, and writing the header row. Refactor shop/views.py to extract that shared scaffolding into ONE helper function that both views call with their filename, header row, and rows; each view should become a thin wrapper. The HTTP behavior of both endpoints must stay byte-for-byte identical (same columns, same ordering, same headers).

urlpatterns = [
    path('export/books.csv', views.export_books_csv),

setup_files.shop/models.py:
from django.db import models


class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    year = models.IntegerField()


class Author(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    country = models.CharField(max_length=50)
setup_files.shop/views.py:
import csv

from django.http import HttpResponse

from shop.models import Author, Book


def export_books_csv(request):
    response = HttpResponse(content_type='text/csv')
    response['Content-Disposition'] = 'attachment; filename="books.csv"'
    writer = csv.writer(response)
    writer.writerow(['title', 'year'])
    for b in Book.objects.order_by('title'):
        writer.writerow([b.title, b.year])
    return response


def export_authors_csv(request):
    response = HttpResponse(content_type='text/csv')
    response['Content-Disposition'] = 'attachment; filename="authors.csv"'
    writer = csv.writer(response)
    writer.writerow(['name', 'country'])
    for a in Author.objects.order_by('name'):
        writer.writerow([a.name, a.country])
    return response

test_setup_files.test_refactor.py:
import os, django
os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'settings')
django.setup()
from django.core.management import call_command
call_command('migrate', run_syncdb=True, verbosity=0)
from pathlib import Path
from django.test import Client
from shop.models import Author, Book

Book.objects.create(title='Zen', year=2001)
Book.objects.create(title='Art', year=1999)
Author.objects.create(name='Woolf', country='UK')
Author.objects.create(name='Borges', country='AR')

c = Client()
r = c.get('/export/books.csv')
assert r.status_code == 200 and r['Content-Type'].startswith('text/csv')
assert r['Content-Disposition'] == 'attachment; filename="books.csv"', r['Content-Disposition']
assert r.content.decode().replace('\r\n', '\n').strip() == 'title,year\nArt,1999\nZen,2001', \
    f'books csv changed: {r.content!r}'

r = c.get('/export/authors.csv')
assert r['Content-Disposition'] == 'attachment; filename="authors.csv"', r['Content-Disposition']
assert r.content.decode().replace('\r\n', '\n').strip() == 'name,country\nBorges,AR\nWoolf,UK', \
    f'authors csv changed: {r.content!r}'

# Consolidation proof: the duplicated response-scaffolding literals must now
# appear at most once in the source (a do-nothing submission keeps two).
src = Path('shop/views.py').read_text()
assert src.count("content_type='text/csv'") <= 1, 'text/csv response construction still duplicated'
assert src.count('attachment; filename=') <= 1, 'Content-Disposition construction still duplicated'
